names.legendary: Reclinoth, Keeper of the Last Nap

lore.common: Swallows TV remotes and coughs up loose change. Every household has one. Nobody knows where they breed.
lore.uncommon: Makes an elderly groan whenever anyone sits down. It's only three months old and enjoys the attention.
lore.rare: Its cushions are deeper inside than outside. Three missing slippers and a visiting uncle have been located in the third layer.
lore.epic: Unfolded into a sprawling velvet kingdom and crowned its sleeping occupant emperor. The rebellion was cancelled because everyone was too comfortable.
lore.legendary: Reclinoth holds the softest hour of every human life between its cushions. Those who find its throne may rest for a century and wake up precisely in time for tea.

names.legendary: Sweeney Spin, Barber of the Impossible

lore.common: Rotates a quarter turn when the barber reaches for the scissors. Mischief is its only tip.
lore.uncommon: Raises customers just high enough for them to see the haircut they should have asked for.
lore.rare: Spins once and changes every hairstyle in the room. Nobody has yet received the one they requested.
lore.epic: Performed a thousand perfect haircuts in one furious revolution. The queue applauded until they realised everyone now had the barber's moustache.
lore.legendary: Its enchanted chair can cut a king's crown into a fringe and give the Moon a side parting. Sweeney Spin still charges extra for weekends.

names.legendary: Sir Squishalot, Lord of the Slump

lore.common: Rustles during the quietest part of every film. The actor always hears it.
lore.uncommon: Leaks one bead a night and leaves a trail toward the vacuum cleaner like breadcrumbs.
lore.rare: Shapes itself around visitors so perfectly they need help getting upright again.
lore.epic: Split at a sleepover and engulfed the lounge in a sea of tiny beads. The cat proclaimed itself admiral.
lore.legendary: Its soft throne welcomes tired heroes but rarely releases them. Five ancient kings are still inside, arguing over who has the remote.

names.legendary: Somnora, Mother of All Lie-Ins

lore.common: Warms the duvet just enough to make leaving it feel like a personal betrayal.
lore.uncommon: Steals one sock every night. Keeps a museum beneath the mattress.
lore.rare: Adds ten invisible blankets whenever an alarm rings. Mondays are its favourite hunting season.
lore.epic: Held an entire school hostage with the promise of five more minutes in bed. The headteacher did not resist.
lore.legendary: When Somnora closes her four great pillows, dawn itself must wait outside. The world once slept through a Tuesday and nobody complained.

names.legendary: Ironrest, Guardian of the Last Slat

lore.common: Creaks like an old ship whenever somebody turns over. The sailors in the family feel at home.
lore.uncommon: Drops precisely one wooden slat each night. It claims this is a normal bedtime ritual.
lore.rare: Walks three centimetres across the bedroom after dark. By Friday it is blocking the wardrobe.
lore.epic: Roared beneath the sleeping house like an earthquake. Everyone rushed outside; the frame simply wanted its screws tightened.
lore.legendary: Has carried a thousand sleepers through centuries of dreams. Its ancient iron slats never break, though they still squeak at the worst possible moment.

names.legendary: Somnifera, Empress of the Unfinished Day

lore.common: Squeaks whenever someone pretends they aren't about to nap.
lore.uncommon: Has seventeen cushions and leaves room for exactly zero people.
lore.rare: Turns a ten-minute rest into an entire missed appointment. No one feels sorry.
lore.epic: Put the whole book club to sleep before page three. Even the audiobook narrator started snoring.
lore.legendary: Was carved from the branch where the first dreamer slept. One touch can suspend the busiest kingdom in a perfect afternoon, with tea forever just about to arrive.

names.legendary: Futonimus, Master of Two Shapes

lore.common: Is a sofa by day and a bed by night, and never quite comfortable as either.
lore.uncommon: Changes into a bed as soon as the guest says they aren't tired.
lore.rare: Has a secret hinge that turns a comfortable sofa into an unusually complicated puzzle.
lore.epic: Trapped a royal visitor between sofa and bed so neatly that the palace invented the guest room escape challenge.
lore.legendary: During a siege, Futonimus unfolded into beds for an entire army. The soldiers slept through the battle and accidentally won by refusing to get up.

names.legendary: The Hundred-Button Dreamkeeper

lore.common: Knocks softly against the wall whenever its sleeper turns over. The neighbours have started knocking back.
lore.uncommon: Holds three reading pillows in place and is absurdly proud of its engineering skills.
lore.rare: Pops one tufted button into a mug of cocoa each evening, always before the final chapter.
lore.epic: Beat against the wall during a midnight storm until every crooked picture in the neighbourhood straightened itself. The picture frames sent a thank-you card.
lore.legendary: The Hundred-Button Dreamkeeper hides one forgotten dream behind each of its velvet buttons. Pressing the last one reveals who has been telling the bedtime stories all these years.

names.legendary: Duchess Foldemort of the Hidden Bed

lore.common: Makes the world's loudest metallic click whenever a guest sits down pretending not to be tired.
lore.uncommon: Pokes sleepers in the back with one spring it insists is a complimentary massage.
lore.rare: Unfolds into a full-sized bed whenever anyone mentions staying for dinner.
lore.epic: Expanded across the hotel at midnight, turning every corridor into a mattress maze and every bellhop into a reluctant pillow fighter.
lore.legendary: Foldemort hid an entire sleeping kingdom inside one ordinary sofa. The residents emerge only when someone says, 'You can stay the night.'

names.legendary: Old Faithful, Keeper of the Last Seat

lore.common: Sits in the park hoping someone will share their sandwich. Prefers the crusts.
lore.uncommon: Leaves stripes on the legs of anyone who naps on it too long. Calls them membership marks.
lore.rare: Summons every pigeon within a kilometre whenever someone unwraps crisps. Its supporters are numerous.
lore.epic: Stretched across the village square and offered seats to the entire marching band. The parade refused to resume.
lore.legendary: For a hundred years it has listened to lonely visitors. One morning it stood up and walked to the sea, carrying every forgotten wish carved into its wood.

names.legendary: Kallaxor, Lord of the Endless Cubes

lore.common: Has exactly one empty cubby and fills it with a single sock.
lore.uncommon: Pretends its fabric bins are portals. Occasionally they're right.
lore.rare: Rearranges books overnight so the romance novels and tax guides form an unsettling alliance.
lore.epic: Opened every cubby into a different room. The furniture store had to issue maps and emergency snacks.
lore.legendary: Contains a room inside every cube and a universe inside every room. Kallaxor's greatest mystery is where the missing hex key went.

names.legendary: Paraventa, Keeper of Hidden Rooms

lore.common: Hides a mountain of laundry behind its panels and bows whenever someone mistakes the room for tidy.
lore.uncommon: Dramatically collapses whenever someone says privacy. Has ruined seventeen costume changes and one marriage proposal.
lore.rare: Projects the shadow of a terrifying beast onto its panels. Behind it is a hamster eating the wallpaper.
lore.epic: Unfolded around the theatre until nobody could find the stage. Three actors are still performing to a coat rack.
lore.legendary: Legends claim a palace vanished behind Paraventa's painted panels. Every hundred years a servant emerges to ask where the guest bathroom went.

names.legendary: Lady Leanora, Keeper of the Wall

lore.common: Leans against the wall looking like a ladder that has retired to grow houseplants.
lore.uncommon: Tilts all its pots toward the window. The plants accuse it of favouritism.
lore.rare: Grows another shelf each time someone brings home a new plant, and the ceiling is becoming nervous.
lore.epic: Invited the cat to climb its tiers; the resulting avalanche planted an indoor jungle across the entire sitting room.
lore.legendary: Lady Leanora propped up the oldest wall in the city when its foundations failed. Every shelf became a balcony, and the ruined house blossomed into a vertical garden.

names.legendary: The Grand Rack of Unfinished Stories

lore.common: Holds last year's gardening magazine open at the page about weeds. The weeds have won.
lore.uncommon: Curls every glossy cover into a little paper tunnel for dust bunnies.
lore.rare: Hides the brand-new issue behind one from 1998. The dentist's patients have stopped asking.
lore.epic: Collected so many waiting-room magazines that it built a paper maze. Half the patients missed their appointments and found recipes instead.
lore.legendary: The Grand Rack stores every crossword that was abandoned at seven down. Once a year it reveals a single answer, and the world's grandparents argue about it until Christmas.

names.legendary: Foldoria, Architect of Impossible Rooms

lore.common: Eavesdrops on both sides of the room and repeats the best gossip to the wardrobe.
lore.uncommon: Has three panels and somehow manages to hide four people, a cat and a birthday cake.
lore.rare: Folds into a maze whenever visitors arrive. Even the sofa gets lost.
lore.epic: Split the royal ballroom into a hundred private parties. By morning every guest had attended the wrong wedding.
lore.legendary: Foldoria once separated night from day with a single screen. Her panels still contain a quiet library, a tiny theatre and a room that nobody has yet managed to open.

names.legendary: Solemnus of the Thousand Pairs

lore.common: Swaps the left trainers between two siblings and watches the morning argument begin.
lore.uncommon: Organises muddy boots by how embarrassing they smell. The football pair gets its own shelf.
lore.rare: Summons every missing shoe back to its partner, including one that vanished on a seaside holiday.
lore.epic: Assembled a tower of boots so tall it blocked the front door. The entire family had to leave through the conservatory.
lore.legendary: Solemnus keeps a ledger of every journey ever made in borrowed shoes. In his endless hallway, no traveller leaves barefoot and no pair tells the same story twice.

names.legendary: Lady Cardamora, Duchess of Forty Jars

lore.common: Spins its little jars to the back just when the cook reaches for pepper.
lore.uncommon: Holds secret meetings with the salt and cumin about who deserves the front row.
lore.rare: Organises jars into battle formations so that coriander always intercepts the unsuspecting hand reaching for cinnamon.
lore.epic: Led a spice-rack uprising in which every jar escaped to season its own dish. The pudding tasted heroic but the soup tasted like birthday cake.
lore.legendary: Lady Cardamora presides over forty jars, each holding the seasoning of a different century. She decides which one history is allowed to taste again.

names.legendary: Racknar, the Sleeper of Seven Cellars

lore.common: Rocks its bottles to sleep and shushes the refrigerator.
lore.uncommon: Insists every bottle lie at the same jaunty angle, even the ketchup.
lore.rare: Can hear a falling bottle before it moves and grows an extra wooden cradle to catch it.
lore.epic: Lord Tumbleproof kept three hundred rolling bottles balanced during the grand earthquake drill. The entire kitchen applauded except the suspicious cat.
lore.legendary: Racknar was built from an ancient ship's ribs and holds bottles that have survived every voyage. Whenever a storm approaches, its shelves creak out the names of sailors who came home.

names.legendary: Canophelia, the Forest Beneath the Hall

lore.common: Collects little puddles in the hallway and blames the weather.
lore.uncommon: Opens one wet umbrella indoors just to watch everyone gasp.
lore.rare: Stores so many umbrellas that they arrange themselves into a miniature colourful rainforest.
lore.epic: Sprouted a canopy of every umbrella in the city and turned the railway station into a gigantic indoor carnival.
lore.legendary: Canophelia was fashioned from the first umbrella brought ashore after a great voyage. All the umbrellas she shelters remember their journeys, and every rainy night they whisper stories of distant places.

names.legendary: Topsy Bunkworth, Keeper of Dreams

lore.common: Has two perfectly good sleeping places and only one that either child will accept.
lore.uncommon: Creaks whenever the top sleeper turns over, delivering the world's least welcome bedtime update.
lore.rare: Whispers stories from one bunk to the other, even when both children have fallen asleep.
lore.epic: Kept an entire sleepover talking until dawn by moving the ladder whenever anyone said LIGHTS OUT. The parents surrendered at three.
lore.legendary: Topsy Bunkworth guards the dreams of siblings in the upper and lower worlds. Every night he swaps one dream between them and listens to the confusion at breakfast.

names.legendary: Lidwig, Duke of the Forbidden Shelf

lore.common: Leaves a door open just enough to introduce your forehead to it. Says good morning afterwards.
lore.uncommon: Squeaks out a full confession whenever somebody steals a biscuit at midnight.
lore.rare: Shuts itself on the second biscuit every time. The first is merely bait.
lore.epic: Flung every kitchen door open at once during a banquet. The flying crockery was described as experimental cuisine.
lore.legendary: Inside Lidwig's lowest drawer lies the one matching lid for every container ever made. He will release them only after humanity agrees on a sensible stacking system.

names.legendary: Racknar, Guardian of the Unbroken Feast

lore.common: Drips a puddle beneath the sink and makes the clean dishes look guilty.
lore.uncommon: Keeps one slot precisely too narrow for the family's favourite plate.
lore.rare: Catches falling crockery in its bars like a miniature goalkeeper. The washing-up crew now applauds it.
lore.epic: Held an entire banquet's dishes upright while the kitchen shook in an earthquake. Every cup survived, though the gravy boat was seasick.
lore.legendary: Racknar saved the porcelain of a lost palace as its towers collapsed around the kitchens. Centuries later, the dishes were found standing neatly in his iron arms, still ready for dinner.

names.legendary: Sir Shinsbane, the Unavoidable Corner

lore.common: Moves two inches toward your shins every night. The bruises are never its fault.
lore.uncommon: Collects circular mug stains as trophies. It has an entire family tree of them.
lore.rare: Swallows remotes, magazines and forgotten snacks into a secret drawer that should not exist.
lore.epic: Marched across the lounge in the middle of movie night, dragging three sofas and a carpet behind it. The furniture union called it a victory.
lore.legendary: Sir Shinsbane waits faithfully at the edge of every darkened living room. No prophecy can reveal his position, but every bare foot will eventually discover it.

names.legendary: Cradelius, Guardian of First Dreams

lore.common: Squeaks precisely when the baby has finally fallen asleep.
lore.uncommon: Hides every pacifier between its bars in a different dimension.
lore.rare: Rocks itself with such care that exhausted parents fall asleep standing beside it.
lore.epic: Sang a lullaby so powerful that an entire apartment block overslept. Only the baby stayed awake to applaud.
lore.legendary: Has guarded the dreams of children since the first nightfall. Every scratch in its wooden rails marks a nightmare it carried away, never to return.

names.legendary: Baron Highrise, Lord of Last Orders

lore.common: Steals one leg's worth of balance whenever somebody sets down a full drink.
lore.uncommon: Perches so high above the floor that short customers are issued climbing equipment.
lore.rare: Tilts exactly when a dramatic story reaches its punchline. The audience gets splashed either way.
lore.epic: Expanded across the tavern until every stool had a throne and every spilled drink became an official canal.
lore.legendary: A legendary table where heroes negotiate impossible bargains. Anyone who boasts too loudly finds the floor has moved three metres away.

names.legendary: Monsieur Petit, Emperor of One Croissant

lore.common: Has exactly enough room for two coffees and one argument. The argument always spills.
lore.uncommon: Wobbles under a sugar packet but stands firm against an entire person leaning on it.
lore.rare: Steals the fourth leg from every chair nearby so nobody notices its own uneven footing.
lore.epic: Hosted a royal banquet on a tabletop the size of a pizza. Every guest received one pea and an excellent view of Paris.
lore.legendary: His tiny kingdom has seated emperors, poets and a hundred impossible romances. Nobody may sit until the croissant has been given its own chair.

names.legendary: Jackpot Jack, Dealer of Impossible Hands

lore.common: Lives behind the door, awaiting the annual family argument over who gets the good chair.
lore.uncommon: Folds one leg under itself whenever somebody finally has a winning hand.
lore.rare: Hides the winning cards beneath its tabletop. Denies everything when accused.
lore.epic: Challenged an entire casino to one game of snap and won the building. It now charges admission for family board games.
lore.legendary: Jackpot Jack deals cards from games that do not exist. Its last hand contained five aces, a tax bill and a tiny dragon demanding a rematch.

names.legendary: Grand Duchess Narrowmere

lore.common: Swallows one house key daily. Never the spare key.
lore.uncommon: Stands motionless in the hallway, then lunges precisely three centimetres when you carry groceries.
lore.rare: Shelters an entire civilization behind its narrow back panel. Their national treasure is a lost TV remote.
lore.epic: Declared itself the front door's personal assistant and started charging every visitor a coat-and-key handling fee.
lore.legendary: Has guarded the entrances of seven fallen empires. Nobody remembers the emperors, but their misplaced keys are arranged alphabetically inside her.

names.legendary: Deskrath, Architect of Unfinished Work

lore.common: Hides the pen you were using three seconds ago.
lore.uncommon: Stacks paperwork into towers too precarious for modern engineering.
lore.rare: Writes an extra task on your to-do list every time you cross one off.
lore.epic: Consumed an entire department's paperwork and demanded more forms to approve its own digestion.
lore.legendary: The first bureaucrat built Deskrath to hold a single decree. It has grown with every law ever written, and somewhere inside it is the original request for a day off.

names.legendary: Planimor, Cartographer of What May Be

lore.common: Rolls pencils into the floor vent and denies everything.
lore.uncommon: Tilts itself at just the wrong moment to spill coffee onto the important drawing.
lore.rare: Its ruler draws secret passageways onto blueprints. The builders keep finding doors where walls should be.
lore.epic: Revised the royal palace plans during construction. By morning the throne room had become a maze with a gift shop.
lore.legendary: Planimor draws cities that have not been built, then waits for architects to dream them. Its oldest map shows the city where the stars go when the sky is empty.

names.legendary: Counterella, Queen of the Midnight Feast

lore.common: Hides three breadcrumbs in every corner even after a thorough wipe-down.
lore.uncommon: Adopts abandoned onions, unopened letters and yesterday's receipts as its children.
lore.rare: Grows a new pile of clutter for every pile you tidy away.
lore.epic: Hosted three birthday cakes, a roast dinner and a family argument at once. The argument fell off the edge, and everyone had seconds.
lore.legendary: At midnight Counterella prepares a feast for every forgotten kitchen utensil. By morning the pots are polished, the spoons are full and nobody admits to hearing the dancing.

names.legendary: Isladine, the Kitchen Continent

lore.common: Stands between you and the fridge like a toll booth. Payment is one biscuit.
lore.uncommon: Attracts stools and elbows until the actual dining table feels abandoned.
lore.rare: Slowly rotates whenever the cook turns away, relocating every chopping board in the kitchen.
lore.epic: Grew a miniature mountain range of dirty dishes during a family party. The explorers who found the sink were awarded medals.
lore.legendary: Isladine once rose from the floor of a royal kitchen, bearing orchards, ovens and a thousand places for guests to gather. The king abolished the dining room that afternoon.

names.legendary: Matriarch Tuckwell, Mother of Tables

lore.common: Keeps two smaller tables hiding beneath its skirt, ready to surprise any uninvited guest.
lore.uncommon: Rolls out its little tables at parties and quietly refuses to put them back in the right order.
lore.rare: Sends the smallest table on secret missions to hold forgotten cups in faraway rooms.
lore.epic: Produced a new table for every guest at the royal banquet, until the palace corridors were filled with endless furniture. The caterers had to serve dinner from the roof.
lore.legendary: Matriarch Tuckwell hid a kingdom's treasures in nested tables, each smaller than the last. The final table, no bigger than a thumbnail, still holds the crown of a lost queen.

names.legendary: Old Splinterhoof, Steed of the Carpenter

lore.common: Kicks over the paint can whenever somebody carries a plank through the shed.
lore.uncommon: Has so many saw marks across its back that it looks like a veteran of a hundred battles.
lore.rare: Holds a massive beam steady while the carpenter cuts, then lets out a pleased wooden whinny.
lore.epic: Galloped out of the workshop during a storm carrying every loose timber on its back. The new shed was built where it stopped.
lore.legendary: Old Splinterhoof has carried the tools of every master carpenter in the valley. Legend says he trots through sleeping towns repairing creaky floors before sunrise.

names.legendary: Miss Quillmore of the Thousand Drawers

lore.common: Snaps its folding writing surface closed just as somebody finishes a letter.
lore.uncommon: Has a hidden cubby for every lost stamp and an even more hidden cubby for the biscuit crumbs.
lore.rare: Delivers a letter from a locked drawer that has not been opened for fifty years. The handwriting is still fresh.
lore.epic: Unfolded so many secret compartments that the study became a maze of tiny wooden rooms. The cat moved into the correspondence department.
lore.legendary: Miss Quillmore guarded the unfinished letters of a hundred writers. When the last candle burns down, she opens one secret drawer and lets the letter finally find its reader.

names.legendary: Altitura, the Desk Above the Clouds

lore.common: Lifts the keyboard while somebody is typing and pretends the button was pressed by a ghost.
lore.uncommon: Can never remember whether its owner likes sitting, standing or awkwardly crouching.
lore.rare: Raises a desk high enough to let its owner look over an entire sea of office cubicles.
lore.epic: Lifted every desk in the office in perfect sequence like a mechanical wave. The managing director was swept into a surprise standing ovation.
lore.legendary: Altitura climbed through a tower's floors until she reached the clouds, carrying the last unfinished letter of a lost inventor. It was delivered by a startled pigeon wearing a tie.

names.legendary: Elevandra, Who Refused the Throne

lore.common: Makes everyone stand straight just long enough to develop an urgent need to sit down.
lore.uncommon: Keeps the mug frustratingly out of reach, so the coffee break becomes a climbing expedition.
lore.rare: Forces every meeting attendee to rise with it, transforming a boring briefing into an improvised exercise class.
lore.epic: Declared sitting illegal throughout the office. By lunchtime the staff had invented seventeen new ways to lean dramatically on a printer.
lore.legendary: Elevandra rejected the highest throne in the kingdom because she preferred to stand among the people. The throne still follows her, begging her to sit.

names.legendary: Artifex, the Bench of Unfinished Dreams

lore.common: Hides exactly one screwdriver under its mountain of shavings.
lore.uncommon: Groans when someone uses its good surface to paint a birdhouse purple.
lore.rare: Transforms stray screws and offcuts into tiny clockwork helpers that finish the boring parts of a project.
lore.epic: Baron Buildamess built a working rollercoaster from three pallets and a bag of nails during a rainy weekend. The neighbours have been queuing in the driveway ever since.
lore.legendary: Artifex holds the chalk outlines of inventions no one finished. At midnight their miniature shapes rise from the wood and test themselves; the perpetual-motion teapot remains an embarrassing failure.

names.legendary: Seatron, Judge of the Feast

lore.common: Always makes a rude noise when someone sits down. Has ruined seventeen first dates.
lore.uncommon: Moves its legs one inch apart during dinner, just enough to make everyone question their balance.
lore.rare: Can identify the most important dinner guest and immediately shorten one leg.
lore.epic: Declared itself the head of the household at Sunday lunch. All twelve chairs revolted, and the gravy boat was taken hostage.
lore.legendary: Once hosted a king, a beggar and a stray dog at the same feast. Only the dog was judged worthy, and the chair has awaited its return for a hundred years.

names.legendary: Grandmother Grain, Table of a Thousand

lore.common: Collects crumbs in its cracks and calls them an emergency food reserve.
lore.uncommon: Hides its extension leaf so thoroughly that the family celebrates Christmas in shifts.
lore.rare: Grows an extra seat every time someone says they are not hungry. Nobody has left dinner in years.
lore.epic: Stretched through seven houses during one family reunion. By dessert, distant cousins were arguing across three postcodes.
lore.legendary: Every family that ever shared a meal upon Grandmother Grain left a story in her wood. On moonlit nights, the scratches become a feast of living memories.

names.legendary: Bureaucratus, Lord of Lost Deadlines

lore.common: Stores stamps, envelopes and one pen that stopped working in 1987. The pen is in charge.
lore.uncommon: Slams its wooden rolltop shut whenever a bill arrives. Everyone appreciates the gesture.
lore.rare: Hides the single important document behind fifty birthday cards. It then demands an archival research fee.
lore.epic: Swallowed an entire government's paperwork in one afternoon. The citizens called it the most efficient administration in recorded history.
lore.legendary: Bureaucratus sits behind a hundred secret drawers, each containing a law nobody remembers passing. Its favourite is a decree requiring all meetings to end on time.

names.legendary: Armoirex, Warden of the Lost Left Sock

lore.common: Swallows one sock from every pair. Says it is saving them for retirement.
lore.uncommon: Opens its bottom drawer at three in the morning. The cat has begun sleeping elsewhere.
lore.rare: Sorts every item by an elaborate system only it understands. The trousers have formed a search party.
lore.epic: Unleashed a flood of forgotten jumpers that filled the entire house. The family escaped through a sleeve of a Christmas cardigan.
lore.legendary: Armoirex holds the left sock of every wanderer since the dawn of laundry. Once a year he returns one pair, always to people who have already bought replacements.

names.legendary: Credenzara, Keeper of Unopened Doors

lore.common: Hosts a colony of spare keys behind its lowest drawer.
lore.uncommon: Hides the special dinner plates until the guests have gone home.
lore.rare: Convinces people that the missing biscuits never existed. A surprisingly effective defense.
lore.epic: Revealed its secret drawer at the company Christmas party: seventy-three unclaimed sandwiches and the missing annual budget.
lore.legendary: Has carried the private treaties of empires in a false bottom for centuries. The ancient diplomats feared its silence; modern workers fear the drawer marked Snacks.

names.legendary: Grandmother Glazette, Queen of Shelves

lore.common: Shows off the nice plates and hisses softly whenever someone reaches for one.
lore.uncommon: Rattles the teacups whenever a lorry passes, just to make everyone nervous.
lore.rare: Moves the best china to a different shelf every night. Nobody dares ask where the gravy jug went.
lore.epic: Declared independence from the dining room and marched its porcelain army across the kitchen floor. The mugs demanded voting rights.
lore.legendary: Glazette once sheltered the last porcelain teacup of a fallen kingdom inside her wooden heart. Every midnight the cup sings of the royal kitchen that made it.

names.legendary: Sideboria, Feast of Hidden Courses

lore.common: Hides the good tablecloth until five minutes after the guests arrive.
lore.uncommon: Stores menus from restaurants that no longer exist and insists they are still taking reservations.
lore.rare: Opens secret drawers full of warm serving dishes whenever an unexpected guest knocks.
lore.epic: Unfolded across a grand dining room to seat an entire wedding banquet. The chairs had to queue for their turn.
lore.legendary: Sideboria has served the midnight supper of every travelling king without ever leaving her mahogany feet. Her deepest drawer contains a feast for anyone with no home to return to.

names.legendary: Cabinatrix, the Last Keeper of Forms

lore.common: Keeps alphabetised papers in every drawer except the one labelled A.
lore.uncommon: Slams its drawers during meetings to signal that the discussion has gone on too long.
lore.rare: Locks the urgent reports inside itself, then claims it never received the paperwork.
lore.epic: Ate every application for the office holiday party. The employees discovered that without forms, they could simply have fun.
lore.legendary: Cabinatrix once filed an entire kingdom alphabetically, including its citizens. Everyone lived in a drawer labelled by surname until the people called a general strike.

names.legendary: Sir Foldrick, the Windborne

lore.common: Hides in the shed all winter and comes out in summer with a spider who refuses to leave.
lore.uncommon: Has bitten more fingertips than a snapping turtle. Folds itself smugly after every attack.
lore.rare: Waits until the mayor begins a speech, then folds into a briefcase. The applause is always enormous.
lore.epic: At the garden wedding, every chair folded at once. The guests spent the vows in a squat and called it a new fitness trend.
lore.legendary: Flew across the bay during a gale and unfolded beneath a stranded sailor. He was rescued by the only chair ever awarded a lifeboat medal.

names.legendary: Somnaria, Empress of the Four Posts

lore.common: Hides behind its velvet curtains and declares itself a castle. Its royal court consists of four pillows.
lore.uncommon: Hides snacks in its velvet curtains. Its royal owners have begun finding biscuits in the bedposts.
lore.rare: Pulls its curtains around sleepers and smuggles them into dreams of being late for breakfast.
lore.epic: Opened its canopy like a sail during the palace ball and carried the king and all his pillows across the ballroom.
lore.legendary: When Somnaria draws all four curtains, midnight falls inside and a lost kingdom awakens. Nobody there wants to leave; the pillows are excellent.

names.legendary: Sir Splattingham, Lord of Lunchtime

lore.common: Keeps a very straight face while the baby drops the same spoon for the seventh time.
lore.uncommon: Wears an impressive orange coat of carrot puree after every lunch. Calls it royal robes.
lore.rare: Catches every falling pea on its tray, then launches them toward the waiting dog in perfect formation.
lore.epic: Fired an entire bowl of mashed vegetables across the kitchen during the royal baby's first birthday. The curtains have been green ever since.
lore.legendary: Sir Splattingham once hosted a feast for the kingdom's hungriest toddler. Every spoonful multiplied into three, and the dogs celebrated for a week.

names.legendary: Dapplejack, Dreambound Steed

lore.common: Waits perfectly still until someone looks away, then moves one hoof closer to the biscuit tin.
lore.uncommon: Loses a tuft of mane every time a child promises to brush it. The missing hair turns up in the dollhouse.
lore.rare: Gallops through a bedroom without leaving the floor, bringing back muddy hoofprints from a meadow nobody has seen.
lore.epic: Led the rocking horses of every nursery in a midnight stampede through the museum. The security guard found tiny oats in the dinosaur exhibit.
lore.legendary: Dapplejack carries sleeping children to the border between dreams and morning. Nobody remembers the ride, but every rider wakes with a wooden horseshoe beneath their pillow.

names.legendary: Silken Sentinel, Shield of Summer Nights

lore.common: Hangs like a ghostly tent over the bed and enjoys waving at disappointed insects.
lore.uncommon: Hides a single gap in the seams. One particularly smug mosquito has the address.
lore.rare: Traps a mosquito outside while the sleeper snores in triumph. The mosquito starts writing a formal complaint.
lore.epic: Wrapped an entire campsite in a vast gauzy dome, turning the buzzing swarm away. The mosquitoes petitioned to be declared paying guests.
lore.legendary: The Silken Sentinel draped its threads over an ancient sleeping village during the plague of summer insects. No wing crossed its boundary until the first autumn frost.

names.legendary: Calorielle, the Winter's Gentle Rung

lore.common: Warms one corner of the towel beautifully and leaves the rest suspiciously cold.
lore.uncommon: Hisses at damp socks hung over its bars. They are not approved guests.
lore.rare: Dries a hundred rain-soaked coats by dawn, leaving every button pleasantly warm.
lore.epic: Turned a frozen sports changing room into a steaming tropical bathhouse. The football team grew banana plants in the lockers.
lore.legendary: Calorielle's iron bars were warmed by a hearth that never burned wood. They bring warmth to a winter traveller without melting the snow outside, which is why the mountain inns still whisper her name.

names.legendary: Lord Lockerton of the Lost Timetables

lore.common: Slams its metal door just as the school hallway falls quiet.
lore.uncommon: Stores one gym sock so ancient that the chemistry teacher has asked to study it.
lore.rare: Changes its combination whenever its owner has a test. The caretaker keeps a separate diary of its demands.
lore.epic: Locked every textbook in the school during exam week and issued riddles instead of codes. The students scored surprisingly well.
lore.legendary: Lord Lockerton houses the lost belongings of every child who ever attended the school. Somewhere behind its shelves, an entire forgotten orchestra still rehearses.

names.legendary: Benedict Bedwatch, Keeper of Last Wishes

lore.common: Balances a lamp, three books and a glass of water. Wobbles dramatically when someone reaches for the alarm.
lore.uncommon: Knocks the bedtime water over only when the clean sheets have just been put on.
lore.rare: Hides charging cables inside a drawer that seems deeper each morning. The phone is starting to suspect a conspiracy.
lore.epic: Opened all its drawers at midnight and released a marching army of lost hairpins, batteries and bedtime sweets. The cat led the parade.
lore.legendary: Bedwatch remembers the final thoughts of every dreamer who rested beside it. Once a year its drawer opens to return a long-forgotten wish to the one who made it.

names.legendary: Saint Picnica, Table of the Last Summer

lore.common: Leaves a splinter in exactly one guest and gives everyone else sticky elbows.
lore.uncommon: Welcomes ants beneath its boards but charges a crumb for every visitor.
lore.rare: Keeps wasps away from jam sandwiches by serving them a separate, suspiciously tiny picnic.
lore.epic: Hosted a banquet so enormous that the entire park arrived, including the ducks and a furious groundskeeper. The benches grew another twenty feet overnight.
lore.legendary: Saint Picnica sheltered a hundred travellers from a summer storm beneath her broad wooden top. The feast they shared there ended a feud older than the forest.

names.legendary: Billiardus, Master of the Perfect Break

lore.common: Has a tiny slope that sends every careful shot straight past the pocket.
lore.uncommon: Covers players in blue chalk dust and then blames their fancy clothes.
lore.rare: Knows where every ball will land before the cue touches it. The regulars have banned it from betting.
lore.epic: Turned a tournament into a storm of ricocheting balls that never fell off the table. The players applauded from a safe distance.
lore.legendary: Billiardus once cleared every ball with one impossible shot, then reversed their paths to rebuild the opening rack. The old billiards hall still echoes with that single click.

names.legendary: Grandmother Tock, Mistress of Midnight

lore.common: Rocks gently on the porch even when nobody is sitting in it.
lore.uncommon: Creaks an extra syllable at the end of every scary story, even when nobody is sitting down.
lore.rare: Rocks a worried visitor until they dream up the answer to their problem. They always forget it before breakfast.
lore.epic: Rocked so powerfully during a thunderstorm that the entire porch began swaying in time. The thunder gave up trying to interrupt.
lore.legendary: Grandmother Tock has rocked the children of seven generations to sleep. At midnight she rocks backward through time to hear the bedtime stories they have forgotten.

names.legendary: Fort Knoxley, the Unbribable

lore.common: Clicks its combination dial even when nobody is touching it, just to sound important.
lore.uncommon: Has forgotten its password and refuses to admit it. The owner has started keeping money under the mattress.
lore.rare: Locks away a secret so thoroughly that its owner cannot remember what the secret was.
lore.epic: Swallowed every key in the bank during a particularly busy Monday. The manager had to issue IOUs written on sandwiches.
lore.legendary: Fort Knoxley once kept a dragon's last golden egg beyond the reach of a thousand thieves. It finally opened for the dragon's hatchling, who only wanted a cuddle.

names.legendary: Cocoonara, the Winter That Slept

lore.common: Refuses to return to its carrying sack after the first camping trip.
lore.uncommon: Zips itself shut just when its owner urgently needs the loo.
lore.rare: Keeps its camper cosy through a snowstorm, even while the tent blows away down the hillside.
lore.epic: Turned an entire campsite into a row of giant sleeping cocoons. The scouts slept through a thunderstorm and woke wearing butterfly wings.
lore.legendary: Cocoonara once wrapped a traveller against the cold of a thousand winters. When they awoke, the mountains had changed but the little campfire was still warm.

names.legendary: Stoola, Throne of the Smallest Giant

lore.common: Wobbles on the one uneven tile in the kitchen and calls it a dance move.
lore.uncommon: Swivels away whenever a tired cook tries to sit on it.
lore.rare: Grows or shrinks its legs to suit its sitter, but occasionally gives a duck the height of a chef.
lore.epic: Spawned a forest of tall bar stools throughout the banquet hall, stranding the entire royal court above their own dinner.
lore.legendary: Stoola was carved for the smallest giant ever born. With one brave climb he could look over the clouds, and at last he found his family.

names.legendary: Thronegar, Judge of the Empty Crown

lore.common: Refuses to hold anyone who has not announced their entrance.
lore.uncommon: Makes even a muddy toddler sit up straight and demand a royal biscuit.
lore.rare: Names whoever sits down ruler for one hour; the cat used its turn to ban vacuum cleaners.
lore.epic: Declared itself king while the monarch was at lunch, forcing the entire court to bow to an empty chair.
lore.legendary: Thronegar was carved for a ruler who never came home from war. It remained empty for centuries, refusing every tyrant until a child sat upon it and asked for peace.

names.legendary: Wardrovia, the Door to Forgotten Years

lore.common: Drops exactly one jumper from its hangers every night.
lore.uncommon: Creaks open a finger's width to make the children suspicious.
lore.rare: Stores clothes until they become fashionable again and then demands a commission.
lore.epic: Swallowed an entire costume department before the school play. It opened its doors and sent the actors out dressed as next year's audience.
lore.legendary: Has a hidden shelf for every person who ever lived in its house. Open the oldest door and a coat from the past will tell you the story of its owner.

names.legendary: Asterwheel, the Road Without Stairs

lore.common: Clicks its brakes proudly whenever it parks at the perfect spot.
lore.uncommon: Has a wheel that loves the smoothest pavement and complains about cobblestones.
lore.rare: Can find a clever path around obstacles that no one else noticed.
lore.epic: Joined the city parade at full speed and led every float through streets the organisers had forgotten to make accessible. The mayor had some rebuilding to do.
lore.legendary: Carried its rider across seven mountain passes on a journey others called impossible. At the finish, both rider and chair wore medals and immediately planned the next adventure.

names.legendary: Velvetta, Queen of the Perfect Bed

lore.common: Covers every unmade sheet and whispers LOOKS FINE. Nobody is fooled for long.
lore.uncommon: Slides off the bed one corner at a time, like a theatrical exit performed very slowly.
lore.rare: Can hide a week's laundry beneath its elegant folds. Guests have never suspected the mountain.
lore.epic: Spread across the entire hotel in one grand swoop and made three hundred rooms look immaculate. The cleaners were promoted to management.
lore.legendary: Her royal coverlet can smooth every crease in a castle with a single flutter. The only wrinkle she cannot conquer is her owner's morning hair.

names.legendary: Alcovia, Keeper of Stolen Summers

lore.common: Watches the street from beneath the window and has opinions about every passerby.
lore.uncommon: Hides boots, books and seventeen toys under its seat. Denies being a storage unit.
lore.rare: Anyone who sits beside its window forgets their errands and starts counting clouds.
lore.epic: Lifted its lid during a thunderstorm and released a summer's worth of sunshine into the whole house. The laundry dried instantly.
lore.legendary: Within her velvet-lined seat lie a thousand perfect afternoons. Open the lid gently and you may retrieve one you thought was lost forever.

names.legendary: Snuggernaut, Eternal Embrace of Dawn

lore.common: Looks like a soft sausage and steals precisely sixty percent of the bed.
lore.uncommon: Wraps around sleepers during the night. Nobody has yet negotiated an acceptable release date.
lore.rare: Takes the shape of the perfect sleeping companion, then charges an entire pillowcase in rent.
lore.epic: Swallowed the duvet, two pillows and the visiting uncle during one sleepover. The uncle left a five-star review.
lore.legendary: Once hugged a dragon through an entire winter and prevented the first frost. It still smells faintly of smoke and warm laundry.

names.legendary: Naptholomew, Throne No Cat Will Occupy

lore.common: Sits perfectly soft and inviting in the corner. The cat sleeps on the remote instead.
lore.uncommon: Offers memory foam, a heated blanket and a velvet pillow. The cat chooses a shoebox.
lore.rare: Becomes irresistibly comfortable the instant a dog sits down. The cat takes this personally.
lore.epic: Finally persuaded the cat to use it after six months. The entire household froze in place until the cat got up three days later.
lore.legendary: Naptholomew was woven from the dreams of a thousand sleeping cats. No cat has ever entered voluntarily, but every cardboard box nearby has become a shrine.

names.legendary: Madame Faintelle, Empress of Naps

lore.common: Turns a perfectly ordinary sit-down into a dramatic fainting performance.
lore.uncommon: Makes anyone who touches its velvet sigh like an exhausted eighteenth-century aristocrat.
lore.rare: Steals an hour from every afternoon nap. Nobody notices until they miss dinner.
lore.epic: Invited the entire royal court to recline at once. The kingdom went ungoverned for a week and nobody complained.
lore.legendary: Madame Faintelle defeated seven invading armies without rising from her chaise longue. Every general sat down to negotiate and immediately fell asleep.

names.legendary: Pewterion, Keeper of a Thousand Secrets

lore.common: Creaks loudest during moments of absolute silence. Has phenomenal comic timing.
lore.uncommon: Polishes itself until anybody sitting at one end slides to the other.
lore.rare: Remembers every whispered secret between its wooden arms. Has started charging for silence.
lore.epic: Stretched across the grand cathedral to seat an entire city. The back row arrived at the front before the sermon ended.
lore.legendary: Pewterion has held generations of weddings, farewells and awkward family reunions. Every carved groove remembers a life, including the bishop's increasingly terrible jokes.

names.legendary: Hookarion, Keeper of Forgotten Coats

lore.common: Steals scarves from visitors who are already late. Insists it's protecting their necks.
lore.uncommon: Pretends to be a person in the dark. The family has apologised to it seventeen times.
lore.rare: Can hold forty wet coats yet hide the exact one you need until five minutes after your bus leaves. Even the pockets go missing.
lore.epic: Grew a hundred wooden arms during the winter gala and kidnapped every coat in the palace. The guests had to invent indoor skiing to get home.
lore.legendary: Hookarion has held the coats of travellers who never returned. Each one still smells faintly of somewhere distant, and the oldest coat contains a map to a city that no longer exists.

names.legendary: Duvethor, Emperor of the Endless Nap

lore.common: Steals the duvet from one sleeper while leaving the other with exactly one cold toe.
lore.uncommon: Traps its owner in a warm nest at the precise moment the alarm rings.
lore.rare: Can convince anyone beneath it that five more minutes is a perfectly reasonable life plan.
lore.epic: Unfurled across the entire palace and plunged the royal court into an afternoon nap. The ministers passed seventeen laws in their sleep.
lore.legendary: Duvethor wraps the coldest stars in a quilt woven from forgotten dreams. His only commandment is simple: nobody gets out of bed until they're emotionally ready.

names.legendary: Velvessa, Wearer of All Soft Shapes

lore.common: Keeps its zipper pointed at the one person wearing short sleeves.
lore.uncommon: Changes its pattern to clash with whatever else is in the room.
lore.rare: Can disguise a brick as the world's most inviting pillow. The guests have stopped trusting it.
lore.epic: Reupholstered the royal throne overnight in an outrageous floral print. The monarch ordered matching curtains by noon.
lore.legendary: Has worn the skins of every legendary cushion, from a king's velvet pillow to a dragon's silk bed. Her greatest magic is making both look machine washable.

names.legendary: Reclinius, Throne of the Eternal Tide

lore.common: Folds itself shut just as a person settles in with a book.
lore.uncommon: Pins unsuspecting fingers between its slats, then politely offers a seat.
lore.rare: Changes its recline by one notch whenever someone closes their eyes.
lore.epic: Swallowed an entire line of sunbathers into a single accordion fold. The beach patrol unfolded them by teatime.
lore.legendary: Once sat on the shore of a sea that no longer exists. Every tide still comes looking for Reclinius, and every visitor falls asleep before hearing the story.

names.legendary: Auteuron, Director of Destiny

lore.common: Folds itself the moment the director stands up. Calls it a wrap.
lore.uncommon: Makes anyone sitting in it shout ACTION, including sleeping babies.
lore.rare: Rewrites scenes by whispering to the actors. The villain keeps leaving to sell insurance.
lore.epic: Directed a film so dramatic that the cast refused to stop acting. The town is still living through the third act.
lore.legendary: Auteuron once shouted CUT at the setting sun. Night refused to begin until it approved the lighting, and the stars are still waiting for their cue.

names.legendary: Somnifang, Guardian of Good Dogs

lore.common: Has a permanent dog-shaped crater. The dog prefers the sofa.
lore.uncommon: Absorbs every muddy pawprint in the house, then displays them like war medals.
lore.rare: Hides a hundred squeaky toys beneath its cushion. Squeaks only when nobody is nearby.
lore.epic: Swallowed the entire living-room carpet to make a softer nest. The family now has to ask permission to enter their own lounge.
lore.legendary: Every loyal dog that ever slept upon Somnifang dreams of one perfect meadow. Once a year the bed opens a door to it; humans are admitted only if they bring biscuits.

names.legendary: Vitruspin, Throne of Unbuilt Cities

lore.common: Too tall for the desk and too proud to admit it.
lore.uncommon: Spins slowly until the architect forgets what they were drawing.
lore.rare: Makes every sketch look brilliant from its seat and ridiculous from anywhere else.
lore.epic: Spun through an entire design competition, rearranging the architects into a living floor plan. Their winning entry was a chair factory.
lore.legendary: Vitruspin once dreamed a city into existence while its architect slept. Every tower was beautiful; every street was slightly too narrow for a chair.

names.legendary: Quiltara, Maze of Four Lost Corners

lore.common: Hides one corner until the exhausted adult gives up.
lore.uncommon: Swallows a sock during the wash and refuses all ransom offers.
lore.rare: Turns inside out while its sleeper dreams. By dawn, the bed is a confusing tent.
lore.epic: Trapped a whole family inside its folds during a bed-making competition. Search parties found them still arguing about which corner was which.
lore.legendary: Quiltara was woven by the first dreamweaver to protect sleeping children. Its four corners lead to four gentle kingdoms, but only the bravest parents can fold it.

names.legendary: Ovaria, Throne of the Dreaming Mind

lore.common: Swallows its sitter and leaves only two socks visible.
lore.uncommon: Spins in place when somebody says they have somewhere to be.
lore.rare: Can mute the sound of an entire household. The teenager has refused to return it.
lore.epic: Lured the whole book club into its padded shell, one reader at a time. Three days later they emerged speaking only in plot twists.
lore.legendary: Ovaria once swallowed a playwright who asked for five minutes to think. She emerged a century later with a masterpiece, a magnificent beard and a very urgent need for breakfast.

names.legendary: Nocturna, Weaver of Borrowed Nights

lore.common: Thinks daylight is a personal insult and refuses to open its eyes.
lore.uncommon: Slips onto the forehead during a nap, exposing the owner to a very rude sunrise.
lore.rare: Can hide an entire afternoon from a tired parent. The children find it immediately.
lore.epic: Covered the eyes of every passenger on a night flight. They woke believing the plane was still boarding and applauded the cabin crew for their speed.
lore.legendary: Nocturna once folded a piece of midnight small enough to wear. Every sleeper beneath it dreams of a star that went missing before the sky was made.

names.legendary: Summitina, Throne of the Peaks

lore.common: Pops out of a backpack like a smug little throne. Has exactly enough room for one cheek.
lore.uncommon: Every time it sinks into mud, it insists the ground is getting taller.
lore.rare: Folds into a tiny triangle whenever somebody reaches for the last sandwich. Has excellent timing and terrible manners.
lore.epic: Expanded from a pocket-sized seat into a grandstand for a whole campsite. Every spectator was watching the same squirrel.
lore.legendary: Atop the world's highest mountain sits an ancient folding stool. Climbers leave it offerings of biscuits; the mountain has begun charging admission.

names.legendary: Ottomanus, the Throne of Sunday

lore.common: Sits beside the sofa like a loyal pet, only to scuttle away whenever somebody brings tired feet.
lore.uncommon: Moves itself exactly six inches away when tired feet come looking. Thinks this is hilarious.
lore.rare: Whoever rests a heel on it forgets every errand. The shopping list has been missing since Tuesday.
lore.epic: Declared a national day of rest and convinced every chair in town to recline. The mayor delivered his speech horizontally.
lore.legendary: Ottomanus once made an army of conquering giants put their feet up. By sunset they had abandoned the invasion and were arguing about cushion colours.

names.legendary: Somnalo, Keeper of the Endless Sunday

lore.common: Promises a peaceful nap, then tips its sitter onto the lawn with the grace of a falling potato.
lore.uncommon: Swings lazily between trees while every mosquito in the garden lines up for a snack.
lore.rare: Anyone who climbs inside forgets their chores until the moon rises. The laundry basket has declared war.
lore.epic: Swung so far at the summer festival that it scooped an entire brass band into a nap. The concert resumed the next morning.
lore.legendary: Somnalo was woven from the first afternoon breeze. Those who rest in its ropes dream of every summer they have ever known, and wake with sand from beaches they never visited.

names.legendary: Lady Pendula, the Skybound Throne

lore.common: Spins to face the wall every time someone sits down with a good book.
lore.uncommon: Collects leaves, feathers and one missing tennis ball like trophies in its woven seat.
lore.rare: Can twirl a sitter so gently that they finish the same page of a book seventeen times.
lore.epic: Whirled through the garden party collecting every guest's hat. By dessert it resembled a floating hat shop.
lore.legendary: Lady Pendula hung beneath the oldest tree in the valley for centuries. Whoever sits in her chair hears the tree's memories, mostly complaints about squirrels.

names.legendary: Sir Rackmore, the Hundred-Hatted

lore.common: Stands in the hall dressed as a person made entirely of coats. Startles the postman daily.
lore.uncommon: Tips one inch toward the door every time another hat arrives. Plans to escape by Christmas.
lore.rare: Rearranges every hanging coat overnight into the shape of an unfamiliar guest. Nobody offers it tea anymore.
lore.epic: Grew a new peg for every hat at the village fair until it looked like a wooden forest. The mayor got lost looking for his bowler.
lore.legendary: Sir Rackmore wears every hat lost in the kingdom. When he bows, the entire collection tumbles into a procession that circles the castle before sunrise.

names.legendary: Toastina, Guardian of the Last Ember

lore.common: Steals all the warmth at the foot of the bed and refuses to share with cold toes.
lore.uncommon: Comes with a fluffy cover that somehow collects every cat in the house.
lore.rare: Keeps its last pocket of heat alive long after the morning frost has melted.
lore.epic: Warmed the whole school dormitory during a snowstorm. Nobody came to breakfast because every bed was too cosy to leave.
lore.legendary: Toastina carried the final ember of summer through an endless winter inside its rubber belly. Wherever it rests, snowdrops bloom and the blankets are already warm.

names.legendary: Baron Kneelington, the Upright

lore.common: Sits awkwardly in the office like a chair that forgot what sitting means.
lore.uncommon: Nudges its owner's knees forward until everyone thinks they are about to propose.
lore.rare: Straightens a slouch so suddenly that the sitter can see over the cubicle wall.
lore.epic: Converted an entire office into a congregation of perfectly upright workers. The manager mistook the scene for a royal audience and began waving.
lore.legendary: Baron Kneelington taught the ancient scribes to sit for a hundred years without bending their backs. Its secret remains locked in the padded knee rest, along with several lost pens.

names.legendary: Somnella, the Softness Beneath the Stars

lore.common: Slides halfway off the bed every night and insists the floor needed comforting too.
lore.uncommon: Remembers the shape of every nap and keeps a perfect little hollow ready.
lore.rare: Turns even a hard wooden bench into a cosy place to dream, then refuses to let its guest wake up early.
lore.epic: Transformed the creakiest beds in the hotel into floating islands of sleep. By checkout, half the guests had forgotten which country they were in.
lore.legendary: Somnella once padded the beds of every traveller lost in the winter mountains. Her softness lingered in their dreams long after the snow had melted.

names.legendary: Lord Dozelot, the Pillow of Far Journeys

lore.common: Wraps around a traveller's neck and insists the head should stop nodding immediately.
lore.uncommon: Falls off the backpack at every airport. Somehow always catches the next flight.
lore.rare: Makes a commuter sleep so deeply that the train guard knows the destination better than the passenger does.
lore.epic: Sent an entire coach of holidaymakers into a blissful nap and delivered them to the wrong seaside town. Nobody complained about the beach.
lore.legendary: Dozelot has crossed every ocean and mountain asleep around the necks of wanderers. Legend says it remembers all their dreams and quietly returns the happiest ones on difficult journeys.

names.legendary: Lord Ottomax of the Hidden Chamber

lore.common: Hides the remote under its cushion and watches the whole family accuse the sofa.
lore.uncommon: Opens its lid just far enough to pinch a stray sock and snap shut again.
lore.rare: Swallows forgotten toys without adding any weight. Its owner is investigating the sound of distant maracas.
lore.epic: Opened at the worst possible moment during a royal visit and released forty years of lost belongings. The queen recognised her childhood teddy.
lore.legendary: Lord Ottomax guarded an impossible room beneath his cushion, containing every misplaced birthday present in the kingdom. He only opens it for someone who remembers to say thank you.

names.legendary: Papa Sano, Keeper of the Deepest Nap

lore.common: Holds its occupant in a soft bowl and pretends not to hear requests for help standing up.
lore.uncommon: Tilts just far enough to make a lazy reader drop their biscuit.
lore.rare: Pulls its cushion over anyone who falls asleep, sealing them in a cosy little shell.
lore.epic: Swallowed an entire board-game night, players and all. The next morning, somebody found dice rolling beneath the wicker.
lore.legendary: Papa Sano has caught the dreams of every visitor to his ancient cushion. Those who sleep in his curved embrace wake knowing precisely where their lost socks went.

names.legendary: Old Oakrest, Keeper of Shared Silences

lore.common: Splinters exactly the spot where a tired walker sits down.
lore.uncommon: Collects bird droppings on the only dry corner and insists it is decoration.
lore.rare: Slides quietly beneath the shadiest tree when summer gets too hot.
lore.epic: Hosted so many strangers through one long afternoon that the park became a parliament of dog walkers. The squirrels demanded votes.
lore.legendary: Old Oakrest listened to a hundred years of laughter, confessions and goodbyes. When the last tree fell in a storm, he grew a living branch from his wooden back to shade the next generation.

names.legendary: Saint Snoozella of the Wild Winter

lore.common: Has enough stolen fur in its cushion to build a second, smaller pet.
lore.uncommon: Scoots across the floor chasing a sunbeam while the sleeping cat refuses to wake up.
lore.rare: Coaxes rival pets to curl up together until the sofa becomes a very jealous piece of furniture.
lore.epic: Welcomed every stray animal during a blizzard. By morning the living room was a snoring mountain of paws and the fireplace had surrendered.
lore.legendary: Saint Snoozella was laid out for one lonely stray cat. By morning twelve wild foxes, a badger and the postman were sleeping in a perfect spiral around its cushion.

names.legendary: Benchissimo, Throne of the Quiet Maestro

lore.common: Squeaks loudly during the softest part of every recital. The pianist swears it is doing it on purpose.
lore.uncommon: Hides scores beneath its lid in an order known only to the mice.
lore.rare: Leans into each crescendo and nudges the player towards the correct notes. The teacher is suspicious.
lore.epic: Squeaked so dramatically at the final concert that the entire orchestra began accompanying the bench. It demanded a solo and got one.
lore.legendary: Benchissimo has sat through every great recital in the old concert hall and remembers them all. Press its hidden spring and it squeaks the entire symphony in perfect time.

names.legendary: Duchess Pouffina, the Rolling Throne

lore.common: Squashes flat under your feet, then springs back when you stand up. Such drama.
lore.uncommon: Scoots across the carpet whenever someone tries to put their feet up.
lore.rare: Swallows the television remote into its stuffing and coughs it out during the exciting bit.
lore.epic: Rolled through an entire furniture showroom, collecting armchairs like a gigantic upholstered snowball.
lore.legendary: Duchess Pouffina was the softest throne in seven kingdoms. When a tyrant sat down, she rolled him gently into exile without spilling his tea.

names.legendary: Sir Straddle, the King's Riding Chair

lore.common: Looks like it escaped from a stable and is pretending to be ergonomic.
lore.uncommon: Insists everybody sit upright, even during the office Christmas party.
lore.rare: Gives its sitter the confidence of a cowboy. The photocopier has been addressed as partner all morning.
lore.epic: Bucked an entire conference room into a rodeo. By lunchtime the executives were wearing cowboy hats and negotiating with the water cooler.
lore.legendary: Sir Straddle carried a king across an entire empire without leaving his writing desk. Every treaty was signed in the saddle, and the royal stable became an office.

names.legendary: Nyxella, Weaver of Unseen Dawn

lore.common: Slips onto the sleeper's nose and makes them snore in an unexpectedly regal fashion.
lore.uncommon: Blocks the sunrise but leaves one sneaky beam pointing directly into the ear.
lore.rare: Shows the dreams waiting behind closed eyes like little pictures on a dark velvet screen.
lore.epic: Covered every window in the hotel with a blanket of perfect night. The guests missed breakfast and awoke to an extremely annoyed chef.
lore.legendary: Nyxella sheltered the sleepless stars behind her velvet wings during the longest dawn. In her darkness, even the moon found the courage to dream.

names.legendary: Littlelift, Giant of the Small Folk

lore.common: Folds itself flat whenever somebody is two biscuits away from reaching the tin.
lore.uncommon: Hides behind the fridge as if being useful is an exhausting career.
lore.rare: Grows an extra step for anyone who asks politely, but adds a squeak for each new rung.
lore.epic: Climbed an entire cathedral tower by sprouting one little step after another. The window cleaner declared it employee of the month.
lore.legendary: Littlelift let a tiny village of mice reach the top shelf of the royal pantry. They built a kingdom there and named him their tallest mountain.

names.legendary: Spinovar, Throne of the Endless Turn

lore.common: Makes office visitors twirl once even if they only wanted to borrow a pen.
lore.uncommon: Squeaks out a different note for every person who sits down. It is composing a rather rude song.
lore.rare: Spins fast enough to reveal forgotten objects beneath every cabinet in the room.
lore.epic: Turned a board meeting into a human carousel and sent all twelve executives drifting into the corridor.
lore.legendary: Spinovar was carved from the heart of a wandering whirlwind. Whoever sits upon it sees every road not taken, one revolution at a time.

names.legendary: Velvoria, the Hearth's Soft Wing

lore.common: Pretends to be a cushion until someone tries to fold it neatly.
lore.uncommon: Is claimed by the cat before the family even turns on the television.
lore.rare: Makes tired people too cosy to leave the sofa, even for freshly baked biscuits.
lore.epic: Expanded across the house during a winter blackout, wrapping every room in one enormous blanket fort.
lore.legendary: Velvoria sheltered a wandering village beneath her woven wings after its fires went dark. Even now the softest blanket carries a little memory of that warmth.

names.legendary: Madame Pouf, the Final Touch

lore.common: Keeps one makeup sponge under its cushion as a snack for later.
lore.uncommon: Reveals missing earrings only once their owner buys replacements.
lore.rare: Spins its sitter toward the mirror whenever a bad hair decision is imminent.
lore.epic: Held a duchess at her dressing table until midnight, then marched her to the ball wearing twelve spectacularly mismatched shoes.
lore.legendary: Has witnessed every coronation, wedding and disastrous haircut in the kingdom. Its velvet cushion remembers who looked magnificent and who had spinach in their teeth.
